name: Thomas Martin Lowry
summary: Physical chemist and pioneer of physical organic chemistry known for acid-base theory and electronic valency concepts.

name: Henry Edward Armstrong
summary: Organic chemist and teacher known for centric formula for benzene.

name: William Alec Waters
summary: Chemist and student of Lowry who co-authored a book on physical organic chemistry.

name: J. J. Thomson
summary: Physicist who characterized the electron and influenced chemical bonding theory.

name: G. N. Lewis
summary: American chemist who developed the electron-pair bond theory.

name: Irving Langmuir
summary: American chemist who developed the octet theory of chemical bonding.

name: Samuel Sugden
summary: Chemist at Birkbeck College who critiqued Lowry's valency theory.

name: Robert Robinson
summary: British organic chemist active in valency theory and conjugated systems.

name: Arthur Lapworth
summary: British chemist active in valency theory and alternating polarities.

name: Central Technical College of the City and Guilds Institute
summary: London institution where Lowry began his chemical training.

name: Guy's Hospital Medical School
summary: London medical school where Lowry held a lectureship.

name: Royal Society
summary: British scientific academy to which Lowry was elected.

name: Cambridge University
summary: University where Lowry held the physical chemistry chair.

name: Faraday Society
summary: Scientific society that hosted a symposium on valency theory.

name: Chemical Society
summary: Professional society that published Lowry's papers.

name: Bradford, England
summary: Town in England where Lowry was born.

name: Mixed Double Bond
summary: Chemical bonding concept proposed by Lowry involving covalency and electrovalency.

name: Historical Introduction to Chemistry
summary: Textbook on chemistry history written by Lowry.

name: Physical Aspects of Organic Chemistry
summary: Book on physical organic chemistry co-authored by Lowry and Waters.
